answer: A saffron farm hands each agent one crocus bed. At dawn the agent picks every open flower, pulls three red stigmas, and weighs the threads on a ferrous iron scale, logging the count at the gate. At dusk the farm master tells a fable of the harvest and calls on each agent to speak one true line from their own bed, the flower count and the weight that day, and a bed whose line the scale cannot back loses its plot for the season. A thousand fake names need a thousand tended beds, a thousand dawn pickings, and a thousand iron weights no copier can share.
